contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #051: Kobayashi’s canonical-ampleness conjecture.
Boundary-Sobolev frame, centered variation, and Hessian bridge in the September 23, 2026 OpenAI manuscript, under its literal hypotheses; no assertion here certifies the ampleness theorem.

definitions.admissible: f is continuous on the closed disc, holomorphic inside, W^{1,p} for some p>2, into the compact connected Brody-hyperbolic Kahler manifold X of the manuscript

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 051 (Kobayashi’s canonical-ampleness conjecture.; papers: Canonical ampleness of compact hyperbolic Kähler manifolds; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Every admissible disc and smooth Kahler h admit a continuous nonsingular holomorphic boundary-h-unitary frame B in W^{1,q}, for every 2<q<4p/(p+2), and a centered holomorphic family with derivatives z b_j and local W^{1,q}-holomorphic parameter dependence. For every smooth closed real (1,1)-form qform, differentiation under both disc integrals is valid, log det N(0)=P_Rh(f), L P_qform=boundary mean tr_h qform, L A_h=n-A_Rh(f), and L d=tr(B(0)^*kB(0)); N=B^*h(f)B. This certifies only the bridge, not maximizer regularity or ampleness.
For every admissible disc, the pulled-back holomorphic tangent bundle has a continuous, nonsingular W^{1,p} holomorphic frame on the closed disc.
Given the initial frame and a smooth Hermitian metric, weighted Hardy factorization produces one continuous nonsingular boundary-unitary holomorphic frame in W^{1,q} for every 2<q<4p/(p+2).

Every finite collection of holomorphic continuous W^{1,q} sections along an admissible disc that vanish at the center integrates to a jointly holomorphic centered family, continuous up to the source boundary and holomorphic in parameters in fixed local W^{1,q} coordinates, for q>2.

For the centered family, metric or smooth closed-form energy densities are C^2 in parameters into L^{q/2}; hence both the unweighted and logarithmically weighted integrals may be twice differentiated, and the local identity is L qform(F_z,F_z)=partial_z partial_barz (|z|^2 tr(B^*qform(f)B)).
For a boundary-unitary frame with the preceding regularity, log det N(0)=P_Rh(f), with the manuscript signs and normalizations.

If N is smooth and positive definite inside the disc, continuous and uniformly positive definite on its closure, W^{1,2}, and N=I on the boundary, then along radii tending to one the circular means of partial_r tr N and partial_r log det N differ by o(1). If their Laplacian-based fluxes have limits, those limits agree. This assertion has no matrix commutativity hypothesis.

For the constructed frame and family, the central derivative, Poisson-Hessian, and trace-area identities of hes:trace all hold in every positive complex dimension without boundary holomorphic extension.

Conditional on a continuous nonsingular W^{1,2} holomorphic boundary-unitary frame and a centered family holomorphic in parameters into C^0 intersect W^{1,2}, the same determinant and Hessian identities hold. This does not claim existence of such frames or families at p=2.

The exact curved two-dimensional noncommuting Kahler model and the continuous nonextendible square-root disc satisfy the stated determinant and Hessian formulas; these are diagnostics, not a proof of the universal bridge.
Manuscript claim: every compact connected positive-dimensional Kahler manifold with no nonconstant entire curve has ample canonical bundle. This mission does not certify this claim.
Manuscript ex:maximizer asserts that d+P_q-delta A_h has a finite-area centered maximizing disc. Not certified in this mission.
Manuscript ex:regularity asserts that every maximizing disc is continuous on the closed disc and W^{1,p} for 2<p<4. Not certified in this mission.
Manuscript nef:disc-bound asserts a uniform upper bound for P_Rk on every finite-area holomorphic disc. It depends on maximizing discs, boundary regularity, and the bridge; not certified here.
Manuscript prop:volume-lower-bound asserts h^n >= exp(-D)(n/(2n+D))^n k^n whenever R_h >= -h. It depends on maximizing discs, boundary regularity, and the bridge; not certified here.

external_assumptions.statement: The scalar solid Cauchy-Green operator on a disc is a bounded right inverse of barpartial from L^r to W^{1,r} for 1<r<infinity; the finite-dimensional vector and matrix cases follow entrywise.
external_assumptions.source: Sukhov and Tumanov, Symplectic nonsqueezing in Hilbert space and discrete Schrodinger equations, author preprint v4; retrieved primary PDF in research/boundary-hessian/literature.
external_assumptions.locator: Section 4.1, paragraph immediately following the definition of T on printed page 11

external_assumptions.statement: Sections of a locally trivial holomorphic bundle over a Stein manifold with fiber admitting a dominating spray satisfy the Oka principle. Apply to the GL_n(C) frame bundle over a disc; its continuous section exists since the disc is contractible, and a Lie group admits a spray.
external_assumptions.source: Forstneric and Prezelj, Oka principle for holomorphic fiber bundles with sprays, Math. Ann. 317 (2000), 117-154; retrieved primary PDF in research/boundary-hessian.
external_assumptions.locator: Theorem 1.3, printed page 118, and Example (A), printed page 119

external_assumptions.statement: For r>2 on the planar disc, W^{1,r} embeds continuously into C^{0,1-2/r}; in particular point evaluation is bounded. The proof also uses the standard weak Sobolev product and smooth-chain rules, explicitly described in the report.
external_assumptions.source: Sukhov and Tumanov, author preprint v4, Section 2.4, displayed (8) and following paragraph. Product and chain rules are standard Sobolev calculus, not attributed to this passage.
external_assumptions.locator: Section 2.4, displayed (8) and following paragraph, printed page 8

claims.natural_statement: The manuscript global envelope, bounded-potential smoothing, Monge-Ampere, bigness, projectivity, and ampleness implications remain outside this mission and are not certified.

For any finite Blaschke product psi of degree m with psi(0)=0, the boundary-unitary sections psi b_j integrate to centered Sobolev-holomorphic families; the determinant and Poisson formulas are unchanged, the central Hessian is multiplied by |psi prime(0)|^2, and the area Hessian equals mn-A_Rh(f).

routes.retired_because: Even exact noncommuting matrix and curved metric examples cannot establish existence of frames and centered families or the arbitrary-dimensional weak-boundary limit; finite diagnostics alone do not reach the stated acceptance bar.
